Maya (Product): Quick sync — we need to pick a sequencing approach for the "multi-tenant routing + KV cache" work. Customers A+B requested early access; infra wants low blast radius. Thoughts on RICE-first vs risk-first canary?
Jordan (Eng): I lean risk-first. If we reduce blast radius we can iterate faster. Concrete ask: what rollback metrics and staged percents?
Sam (ML): note: KV cache invalidation can cause tokenization/embedding cache mismatch. If new routing changes cache keys we'll see 1-3% quality regressions initially. Need eval set check before rolling.
Kevin (SRE): Proposal: staged percentages [0.5%, 5%, 25%, 100%] with automatic rollback if either: error_rate > 0.5% over 5m OR p95 latency increase > 30% AND user-facing error > 0.2%. Also health-check traffic to hit warm cache bucket.
Dana (PM): For prioritization, I ran quick RICE for two options: "customer-first" (Reach=40, Impact=4, Confidence=0.6, Effort=6 -> RICE≈16) vs "risk-first" (Reach=30, Impact=3, Confidence=0.8, Effort=4 -> RICE≈18). So RICE slightly favors risk-first but customer ask strong.
Maya (Product): Good data. Tradeoffs: risk-first reduces rollback cost but delays customers. Customer-first reduces time-to-value but higher revert risk. We should pick sequencing that allows allowed early customers + tight guardrails.
Jordan (Eng): Can we do hybrid? Start with a tiny customer-first canary: onboard Customer A at 0.5% of their traffic (or 5% of a canary slice) while running broader risk-first internal canaries.
Kevin (SRE): Hybrid ok if we set clear isolation: dedicated routing tag and separate cache namespace. If we launch Customer A, we force their requests through dedicated pool and use KV namespace prefix `canary:custA:`. Rollback is a tag flip.
Sam (ML): Add an automated quality check job that runs eval prompts against both variants every 15m. If similarity drops beyond threshold (e.g., BLEU-like or embedding cosine delta > 0.08) alert and block progression.
Maya (Product): Sounds reasonable. We need rollout doc + launch criteria. Draft criteria: 1) infra health gates pass for 24h at 25% internal canary, 2) eval quality delta < threshold over 1000 prompts, 3) no customer-visible errors > 3 incidents in 48h.
Dana (PM): Suggest scoring them as Must/Should/Optional for launch. Also call out support plan for Customer A and credit terms if we need a rollback.
Jordan (Eng): I'll sketch the traffic-splitting config. Example nginx map we can gate with rollout-bot:
```
map $http_x_rollout_tag $backend_pool {
  default backend-v1;
  "canary-custA" backend-canary-custA;
}
```
Kevin (SRE): rollout-bot: create canary job with percentages [0.5,5,25,100], health checks, rollback triggers.
rollout-bot: canary job created -> id: cj-2026-0316-42. Monitoring hooks attached (pager + slack).
Maya (Product): Action items: Jordan -> config + runbook, Kevin -> automation for gating + rollback, Sam -> eval harness + thresholds, Dana -> update customer comms and contracts. Target soft-launch to Customer A next Tue if gates pass.
Jordan (Eng): noted. I'll post PR with traffic-split + example test soon.
Sam (ML): I'll queue eval suite and share baseline numbers by EOD tomorrow.
Kevin (SRE): I'll set up the rollback window and test the tag flip path in staging.
Dana (PM): I'll draft the comms and contingency credits.
Maya (Product): Thanks — we'll reconvene Fri for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
